name: Magnetite
physical: Kept nearby for stamina and stability
Linked by crystal healers to feeling anchored and aligned
summary: Magnetite is a black, strongly magnetic iron oxide, often in sharp octahedral crystals, used for grounding, alignment and drawing in what you intend.
intro: Magnetite is the natural magnet. Its black, metallic octahedral crystals pull paper clips, nails and compass needles toward them, and a good specimen from Arkansas or Russia has mirror-bright faces that look cut by hand. In massive form it is dense, dark and heavy, and it is a major iron ore. Grains of magnetite sit in beach sands, along black streaks that cling to a magnet. It is harder than most metals, 5.5 to 6.5, though brittle. Crystal enthusiasts cherish magnetite as a pocket stone that quietly sets things in alignment.
history: The name is thought to come from Magnesia, the region of Greece where magnetic stones were found. Ancient Greeks and Chinese discovered that magnetite stones could attract iron, and the first compasses were made from lodestone, a naturally magnetized form. In China, South-pointing spoons made of lodestone were used for divination and navigation. Magnetite is also found in some bacteria and animals, which use it to sense the magnetic field. It remains vital as an iron ore. As a metaphysical stone, its attraction power made it a symbol of drawing things to you.
meaning: Crystal healers see magnetite as a stone of attraction, alignment and grounded direction. It is linked to the root and earth star chakras, and used to feel stable, centered and clear about what to pursue. Practitioners say it supports manifestation, drawing in what you intend and keeping you on course. The magnetic quality is read as a symbol of pulling opportunities toward you and gently repelling distractions. Emotionally it is said to steady restless nerves and give a sense of inner compass. Traditionally it is associated with balanced energy and stamina. Many people hold it during goal-setting or keep it on the desk when navigating decisions.
howToUse: Hold a magnetite crystal while naming one intention you want to draw toward you, then set it on your desk as a reminder. Carry a tumbled piece on days when you need grounding and direction. Use it in manifestation grids at the center or at north. Place a small piece under your pillow if you want stable, grounded evenings. Keep it away from phones, credit cards and watches, since the magnetism can interfere with them.
care: Magnetite is durable but can rust when wet or exposed to humidity, so keep it dry and avoid soaking. Wipe with a dry cloth. Cleanse with sound, breath, smoke, moonlight or sun. Store away from electronics, magnetic strips and compasses, and keep away from pacemakers or medical devices. Keep a bag of crystals with magnetite separated, as it may attract metallic iron dust from the others.
identify: Genuine magnetite is black, heavy, strongly attracted to a magnet and leaves a black streak. It can be confused with hematite, which leaves a red-brown streak and is only weakly magnetic, with chromite, black tourmaline and manufactured hematine. Magnetite often forms octahedra, while hematite forms rosettes and plates. Fake crystals made of resin or cast metal are occasionally sold, but they lack the true octahedral faces.

faq.a: Yes. Magnetite is the most magnetic naturally occurring mineral, and it attracts iron objects. Some pieces are naturally magnetized and are called lodestones, which were used as early compasses.
In crystal tradition magnetite is used for grounding, alignment and drawing in intentions. People carry it for stability or place it on desks and altars during goal-setting.
It is better not to. Magnetite is an iron oxide and can rust or stain if left wet. Dry it thoroughly if it gets damp, and cleanse with sound, smoke, moonlight or sun instead.
